title: A Hollow for the Sigil
premise: Ada Ashgrove has spent her twenty-two years in Hollowmere, the last valley where the sigil-magic of the old guilds cannot reach, tending a guild house that has forgotten its purpose. When a dying courier named Wren presses a bloodstained map into her hands, Ada learns the guild's founders didn't flee magic—they sealed it, and the seal is failing. Guided by Wren and hunted by the Hollowed King's wardens, Ada crosses a winter-bound country to unbind the true king from the sigil-thing that wears his crown, discovering along the way that she is not the guild's last member but its first heir: the living key to the original seal. In the end, Ada must choose between re-forging the seal with herself at its heart—safe, invisible, alone—and shattering it forever, freeing the king and the world's magic at the cost of the valley's protection; she chooses to break it, returns to a changed Hollowmere no longer hidden but no longer hollow, and opens the guild doors to a country learning what belonging means.
about_author: Cyrus Zhou is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping river valleys before turning to fiction, a trade that left an enduring obsession with borders and the people who live just inside them. They write quiet, wintry fantasy about inherited obligations and the small rebellions that undo empires.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Establishes Hollowmere: fog at the ridgeline, a guild house of nine aging members, and Ada's restless certainty that she was born on the wrong side of the map. She repairs roofs and copies dead members' names into a ledger no one reads. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. During the first snow, Ada finds Wren half-drowned at the ford, clutching a leather tube. The valley's fog, which repels outsiders, let him through—which should be impossible. He is feverish, bleeding from a wound that glows faintly. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding guild law.

chapters.title: What the Fog Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, fever-dream fragments interleaved with Ada nursing him. We learn of the Hollowed King, whose crown-sigil eats memory and will, and of wardens called the Graycloaks sweeping the lowlands. Wren whispers that he was carrying the map 'home.' Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cross-referencing Wren's map against the guild ledger, Ada finds the founder's name matching a mark on the map's heart—and her own surname beside it in the oldest hand. The guild elders refuse to look. Emotional beat: the vertigo of inheritance.

chapters.title: Graycloaks at the Gate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Two Graycloaks arrive under a flag of parley, asking politely for a thief and a stolen map. Elder Maren lies badly. Wren realizes staying means the valley burns. Emotional beat: guilt—the outsider endangering the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Leaving Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Against the elders' vote, Ada volunteers to take the map out through the fog herself, drawing pursuit away. Wren insists on coming despite his wound. Crossing the ridge, Ada feels magic touch her for the first time—like cold water finding a crack. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Kings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Travel through villages where hearth-shrines still hold outlawed sigils. Wren teaches Ada basic warding; her wards bloom too strong, too fast. A Graycloak patrol nearly takes them; a shrine-keeper hides them. Emotional beat: Ada's power as both gift and target.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the smuggler city of Ashmarket they seek the map-dealer Vess, who recognizes the seal-work and goes pale: this is a Founder's Key, and there are three. She offers to buy it; Ada refuses. Emotional beat: temptation—Vess offers Ada a life where she could disappear forever.

chapters.title: The Price of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Betrayal: Vess sells their route to the Graycloaks. A rooftop chase ends with Wren taking a warden's blade meant for Ada. His fever returns worse; the wound is sigil-touched and slowly hollowing him. Emotional beat: love confessed obliquely, at the worst possible time.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. While Wren sleeps, Ada reads his hidden letters: he was the King's own scribe before the crown took him, and he stole the map because the king's true self, buried deep, still sends messages out. Emotional beat: Ada's anger softening into resolve—she is carrying a man's last hope.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the map to a drowned monastery, they retrieve the second key from beneath the flood-chapel altar, guided by Ada's inexplicable instinct for the seal-script. The Graycloaks arrive as the water recedes. Emotional beat: competence earned—Ada stops running and starts choosing.

chapters.title: What the Crown Eats
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Captured briefly by a defector Graycloak, Sera, who shows them a hollowed village: people smiling, empty, crowned with faint sigil-scars. Sera explains the long winter is the crown's harvest. Emotional beat: horror clarifying stakes—the enemy doesn't want them dead, it wants them vacant.

chapters.title: Sera's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The defector agrees to guide them to the capital's underways if they swear to kill the king rather than free him—she believes nothing human remains. Wren, who knew the king, cannot promise. Fractured alliance. Emotional beat: the ethics of mercy versus safety.

chapters.title: Underways
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Descent beneath the capital through sigil-lit tunnels where the founders once worked. Ada's blood resonates with the walls; carvings show a founder pressing her own hand into a seal—her ancestor, her face. Emotional beat: destiny closing like a trap.

chapters.title: The Third Key Is a Person
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the deep archive, Wren deciphers the truth: two keys unlock, the third binds—and the third key is the founder's living heir. The seal was always meant to be remade with Ada inside it. He hides this from her. Emotional beat: protective deception planting the act's betrayal.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They surface into the capital as the final frost begins—streets icing midday, citizens drifting toward the palace like sleepwalkers. Sera realizes the harvest has started early. Emotional beat: clock now audible in every scene; no more detours.

chapters.title: Palace of Smiles
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Infiltration through the servants' warrens. They witness the court: nobles hollowed mid-gesture, a kingdom performing cheerfulness around an empty throne room. Wren's old quarters are preserved like a shrine. Emotional beat: grief for a world already half-lost.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Confrontation in the throne room: the sigil-thing speaks with the king's mouth and offers Ada everything—her valley safe, Wren healed—if she simply hands over the keys. Wren reveals the third-key truth to stop her accepting. Sera moves to kill the king. Emotional beat: every secret detonating at once.

chapters.title: Two Hands on the Seal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax begins: Sera's blade versus the crown's will; Ada seizes the king's hand and the keys flare. Inside the sigil, Ada meets the buried king—a tired man who asks her not to save him at the world's expense. Emotional beat: the choice made flesh.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax resolves: instead of reforging the seal with herself at its heart, Ada shatters all three keys, pouring the founder's binding into the crown itself and burning the sigil-thing out. The king wakes, mortal and weeping; the long winter cracks. Wren's hollowing wound closes. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused, freedom chosen.

chapters.title: After the Frost
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The king, restored but humble, abolishes the crown's claim over sigil-craft; Sera takes command of reforming the wardens. Magic returns to the lowlands gently, hearth by hearth. Emotional beat: exhaustion, tenderness, the strange lightness of a finished task.

chapters.title: A Guild With Open Doors
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Spring in Hollowmere: the fog thins for the first time in centuries, and travelers arrive asking to learn. Ada enters the founder's name and her own in the ledger side by side, then leaves the book open on the table. Wren stays. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited—home as something you build and share.
